items.name: Ampelmännchen
clues: Tourists in Berlin photograph it every day. Most Berliners walk past it without looking.
A traffic psychologist in East Berlin designed it in 1961.
After reunification, many were replaced with a western version, until people started campaigning to save it.
In the 1990s a designer started turning old ones into lamps. Today his company has several shops in Berlin.
A little man in a hat, in red and green. The story goes that the designer added the hat after seeing Erich Honecker in a straw hat on TV.
You see him at pedestrian crossings all over Berlin: green means go, red means stop.

items.name: Motorola Razr
clues: In the mid-2000s, it was the coolest thing you could pull out of your pocket.
It came out in 2004, with a metal body that was amazingly thin for its time.
It sold more than 130 million, but its maker fell far behind when smartphones arrived.
Its maker’s phone business was bought by Google in 2012 and sold on to Lenovo two years later.
It came back in 2019 as a smartphone that folds in half, with a bendable screen.
A Motorola flip phone whose name sounds like something you shave with.

items.name: Crocs
clues: Some people think they are the ugliest shoes ever made. Plenty of those people own a pair.
Three friends from Colorado launched them in 2002 at a boat show in Florida.
After a boom, sales collapsed around the 2008 financial crisis and the company made huge losses.
They came back with fashion collabs, including platform versions on a Paris catwalk in 2017.
Made of soft, light foam, with holes in the top and a strap at the back.
Holey foam clogs that people decorate with little charms called Jibbitz.

items.name: Fila
clues: Your parents might have worn it to the gym. You might wear it to a party.
Two brothers started it in 1911 in a town at the foot of the Italian Alps.
By the 2000s it looked old-fashioned, and in 2007 its Korean branch bought the whole brand.
In 2018 a chunky white trainer it first made in the 1990s was named Shoe of the Year by Footwear News.
In the 1970s a Swedish tennis star won Wimbledon again and again wearing its clothes.
An Italian sports brand with a red and navy “F” logo.

items.name: VW ID. Buzz
clues: Surfers, hippies and families with too many children have all loved the original.
The original first rolled out of a factory in Wolfsburg in 1950.
Production of the old design stopped in Germany long ago, but a version was still being built in Brazil until 2013.
A concept for its return was shown in 2017, and the new one went on sale in 2022.
From the front it looks like the old one, with two-tone paint, but it runs on batteries.
Volkswagen’s electric version of its famous camper van, the Bulli.

items.name: Adidas Samba
clues: In 2023 it felt as if everyone in Berlin under thirty was wearing a pair.
It first appeared around 1950, made to help footballers train on frozen, icy pitches.
For decades it was mostly an indoor football shoe, cheap and practical.
Around 2022 it jumped from the football shelf to the fashion pages, and soon it was everywhere from Paris to Neukölln.
Low and flat, with a light-brown gum sole and a T-shaped panel of leather over the toes.
A trainer with three stripes that shares its name with a Brazilian dance.
